title: Permutation Importance, PDP & SHAP
interviewAnswer: Interpretability tools answer different questions: permutation importance measures performance drop when a feature is disrupted; PDP shows average predicted response; SHAP attributes prediction differences under a chosen background/assumption framework.
why: Permutation Importance, PDP & SHAP is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
deepDive: Interpretability tools answer different questions: permutation importance measures performance drop when a feature is disrupted; PDP shows average predicted response; SHAP attributes prediction differences under a chosen background/assumption framework. Correlated features complicate attribution. Global and local explanations differ. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: Use permutation importance to find useful features, then SHAP for individual high-risk decisions—but state that neither proves causal impact.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.
followUps: When would you not use Permutation Importance, PDP & SHAP?
How would you validate or tune Permutation Importance, PDP & SHAP?
production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
